alt: The global scope holds one name, total, starting at 0. Calling add(x) pushes a local scope holding only x. Because add declares global total, every call changes the same global total instead of creating a local copy, ending at 8 after add(5) then add(3).

steps.caption: Before either call, the global scope has one name, `total`, set to 0. No function is running, so there is no local scope yet.
Calling add(5) pushes a local scope holding only the parameter `x`. `global total` tells Python that `total` inside add refers to the global name, not a new local one.
`total += x` changes the global `total` directly, since `global total` ruled out a local copy. total is now 5. The local scope still only holds x.
add(5) returns. Its local scope, holding only x, disappears. The global total keeps the new value.
Calling add(3) pushes a local scope holding only the parameter `x`. `global total` tells Python that `total` inside add refers to the global name, not a new local one.
`total += x` changes the global `total` directly, since `global total` ruled out a local copy. total is now 8. The local scope still only holds x.
add(3) returns too. The global total ends at 8, changed by both calls, and no local total was ever created.
